item.title: Swedish AI browser Strawberry is now available to everyone
item.description: Stockholm-based Strawberry is launching its “self-driving” AI-powered browser in open beta after a year in closed testing. Strawberry is a browser with built-in AI agents that can surf, click, and perform real tasks on behalf of the user, even on login-protected sites. The idea is to make AI agents available to non-technical users such as salespeople, recruiters, and analysts, without them needing to be able to write advanced prompts or code. item.title: With physical AI, gunslingers and risk takers need not apply
item.description: Agentic AI came on like a storm over the past year or so, but blazed a trail littered with failed projects and cutting-edge high-tech junk that companies are still trying to sort out. So it’s perhaps no surprise that tech industry execs are urging enterprises to move cautiously with physical AI, where mistakes can have far-reaching business and societal consequences. “We need clear boundaries…, definitions, and rules,” said Tianlan Shao, CEO of Mech-Mind Robotics, which makes industrial robots.

item.title: Mistral AI deepens compute ambitions with Koyeb acquisition
item.description: Mistral AI has acquired Paris-based cloud startup Koyeb, marking the model-maker’s first acquisition and entry into the enterprise infrastructure market. item.title: Apple to kill app support for Intel-based Macs next year
item.description: IT admins and decision-makers take note: Apple has confirmed it will terminate Rosetta support for Intel-based apps starting with macOS 28 in 2027. That means any remaining Intel apps your company relies on must be replaced to maintain business continuity and security. item.title: Mistral CEO: AI could replace more than half of companies’ software
item.description: >More than half of the software purchased by companies today could eventually be replaced by AI, Mistral AI CEO Arthur Mensch said in an interview with CNBC. The statement comes at a time when software stocks are under pressure due to concerns that AI will undermine SaaS business models. According to Mensch, a major shift is already happening, with companies increasingly choosing to build their own AI-based applications instead of purchasing traditional SaaS services.
